topics.name: can / cannot for ability and rules

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a correct instruction?
options: Draws the board on a sheet of paper.
Draw the board on a sheet of paper.
Drawing the board on a sheet of paper.
questions.rule: An instruction starts with the base form of the verb: Draw the board.

options: Each player can move one piece at a time.
Each player can moves one piece at a time.
Each player can moving one piece at a time.
questions.rule: After can, use the base form of the verb: can move.
This game is one thing, so the present verb takes -s: needs.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A habit (every morning) takes the simple present. With one person (Arjun), add -s: solves.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After don't, use the base form: don't move.

questions.after: remove one of your opponent's men.
questions.rule: can never takes -s, and it is followed by the base verb: can remove.

questions.after: many pieces does each player get?
questions.rule: To ask about a number of things, use How many.
An instruction starts with the verb: Ask + person + thing.

options: Yes, I play chess every Sunday.
Yes, I plays chess every Sunday.
Yes, I playing chess every Sunday.
questions.rule: With I, the simple present has no -s: I play.
can stays the same and takes the base verb: I can solve.

options: How many pencils Pintu did have?
How many pencils did Pintu have?
How many pencil did Pintu have?
questions.rule: Question order: How many + plural noun + did + subject + base verb.

options: Don't remove men from your opponent's mill.
Not remove men from your opponent's mill.
Don't removes men from your opponent's mill.
questions.rule: A 'don't' instruction is Don't + base verb: Don't remove.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: can never takes -s: a player can fly.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After do in a question, use the base verb: Where do you keep...?
With one person (Mira), the simple present verb takes -s: invents.

questions.after: the smaller number from the bigger one.
questions.rule: Steps of a trick are instructions, so they begin with the base verb: Subtract.
When Who is the subject, the verb comes straight after it: Who makes...?
Subject + can + base verb + object: You can draw the board.

chat: I have a new riddle for you.
questions.rule: In a question, the verb comes before the subject: What is it?

chat: How do I start the number trick?
questions.rule: Giving an instruction? Start with the base verb: Take.
One person takes doesn't, and after doesn't the verb has no -s: doesn't like.

options: You not can remove these men.
questions.rule: The negative of can is cannot + base verb: cannot remove.

options: Why did Pintu give away the box?
Why Pintu gave away the box?
Why did Pintu gave away the box?
questions.rule: Past question: Why did + subject + base verb: Why did Pintu give...?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Riddles and jokes is plural, so the present verb has no -s: exercise.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The second part is an instruction to you, so use the base verb: remove.

questions.after: make a move, he loses the game.
questions.rule: The negative of can is cannot, and it comes before the verb: cannot make.

questions.after: did you learn this number trick?
questions.rule: To ask about a place, use Where. Who and Whose ask about people.
Each player is singular: gets. The number comes before the describing word: nine round pieces.

chat: How does your brother keep fit?
questions.rule: A daily habit with he takes the simple present with -s: He plays.

chat: Can your grandmother do the 1089 trick?
options: Yes, she can does it very fast.
Yes, she can do it very fast.
Yes, she cans do it very fast.
questions.rule: Even with she, can has no -s and takes the base verb: can do.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Pintu invited ten friends and gave each one a pencil.
Pintu invited ten friends and give each one a pencil.
Pintu invite ten friends and gave each one a pencil.
questions.rule: Both actions happened in the past, so both verbs are in the simple past: invited ... gave.

options: Take an orange and share it equally.
Take a orange and share it equally.
Take an orange and shares it equally.
questions.rule: orange starts with a vowel sound, so use an; both instructions use the base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Last week is the past. The past of teach is taught.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After can, always use the base verb, even with two people: can play.
This is the subject of the sentence, so use I: My sister and I can play.

questions.after: you do with the extra pencil yesterday?
questions.rule: yesterday shows the past, so the question uses did.
Who is the subject here, so the past verb follows it directly: Who invented...?
Please + base verb makes a polite request: Please give me...

options: Yes, I finish it before lunch.
Yes, I did finished it before lunch.
Yes, I finished it before lunch.
questions.rule: Answer a Did question in the simple past: I finished.

options: They are in under the bed.
questions.rule: They takes are. Use just one preposition: under the bed.

options: If you has only three men left, they can move to any empty spot.
If you have only three men left, they can moves to any empty spot.
If you have only three men left, they can move to any empty spot.
questions.rule: you have (not has), and after can use the base verb: can move.

options: How did Pintu still have one pencil in the box after giving ten away?
How Pintu still had one pencil in the box after giving ten away?
How did Pintu still had one pencil in the box after giving ten away?
questions.rule: How did + subject + base verb: How did Pintu still have...?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two instructions joined by and both use the base verb: Take ... and write.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does in a question, the verb has no -s: does the answer always come?

questions.before: The trick works only if the first and last digits
questions.rule: digits is plural, so the present verb has no -s: differ.

questions.after: your opponent has no other men, you can remove a man from a mill.
questions.rule: If gives a condition: If this happens, you can do that.
Question order: How many + noun + can + subject + base verb.
Don't let + person + base verb: Don't let your opponent make a mill.

options: You reverses the number, subtract, reverse again and add.
You reverse the number, subtracting, reverse again and add.
You reverse the number, subtract, reverse again and add.
questions.rule: With you, every verb in the list stays in the base form: reverse, subtract, reverse, add.

chat: Can I remove a man from your mill?
options: No, you can't, because I still has other men on the board.
No, you can't, because I still have other men on the board.
No, you can't remove, because I still having other men on the board.
questions.rule: I takes have, not has: I still have other men.
